lessons: Do not take Victim of Night second as I did: it went unplayed in my WR, and the guide's warning about off-colour early removal applied, so stay in colour from pick 2 onward.
Tonight contradicted the guide's WR line: my 0-6 deck with cheap creatures, Rally the Peasants and four fliers lost every game in 17 to 38 turns, so fliers alone were not enough.
Give red eight or nine Mountains: my 10 Plains/7 Mountain WR ran Geistflame, Harvest Pyre, Into the Maw of Hell and two Tormented Pariah, and the guide's warning about 6-7 Mountains applied.
Draft a real graveyard payoff plan: I played Stitched Drake, Makeshift Mauler and Ghoulraiser but left out Ghoulcaller's Chant and Ghoulcaller's Bell, both taken late, so my self-fuel was thin.
Don't spend late picks on Think Twice and Dream Twist, since neither made my deck; take evasive finishers instead, because both of my lost matches went to three games.
My removal (2x Tribute to Hunger, Sensory Deprivation, Corpse Lunge) carried the 2-0 win over WR's Midnight Haunting and Ghostly Possession, so prioritise cheap removal over marginal creatures.

The guide's aggro framing failed tonight: my WG games ran 16 to 32 turns, and with Chapel Geist as my only flier the wide ground plan stalled. Draft evasion and card advantage over extra ground bodies.
Delver of Secrets and Cobbled Wings went unplayed, as the guide predicted, and my late Spare from Evil was cut. Take playable two-drops over these late picks.
Tonight's long games, up to 32 turns, justified 17 lands. The guide's 16-land option for aggressive decks is risky when boards stall.
Against WG in round 1, I sided in Kessig Wolf Run, Trepanation Blade and Undead Alchemist for Kessig Wolf, Traitorous Blood and Typhoid Rats, and won the match 2-1.
Round 3 fell 1-2 to WB's removal-heavy grind (Fiend Hunter, Smite the Monstrous, Rebuke) in 21-29 turn games, so prioritise recursion and card advantage like Ghoulcaller's Chant.
Expect colorless bombs to be contested: seat 2's WG deck also ran Galvanic Juggernaut, which I took first in pack 2.
Contradicting the guide's WB 45% warning, a white-first WB on 11 Plains/6 Swamp went 3-0 with Fiend Hunter, Rebuke, Smite the Monstrous, Voiceless Spirit and Abbey Griffin.
Six removal spells did not hurt against the guide's 'about five' cap: Doomed Traveler, Avacynian Priest and Selfless Cathar curved out, and Rally the Peasants closed the long games.
Committing by mid pack 1 worked: first picks Falkenrath Noble, Corpse Lunge and Voiceless Spirit all made the deck, while the second Woodland Sleuth and Nightbird's Clutches were wasted picks.

Blue-red lost both 0-2 matches in 19 to 24-turn games, so prioritize evasive clock like Spectral Flight and Pitchburn Devils over defensive bodies like Fortress Crab, since my removal-heavy deck never closed games.
The 2-5 game record came against a fast WB deck and a BR deck, so take early pressure over the stall pieces, and don't count on a grindy UR shell to win long games.
The 2-1 win over UG came in a 23-turn game, so blue-red's removal and fliers can beat slower green decks, but only if the board stays under control early.
Tonight contradicted the guide's skip-list: my BR deck ran Wooden Stake and Sharpened Pitchfork, the filler I'd noted to cut, so cut narrow filler like these.
Black flowed, and Dead Weight went first pick in packs 2 and 3; BR won its two 2-0 rounds, so take black removal early.
My 1-2 Round 1 loss came against UG with Spider Spawning and Murder of Crows, while BR had only Vampire Interloper as a flier, so draft more evasion or answers.
Keep the second Lost in the Mist rather than cutting it: our games ran 15 to 34 turns, and we lost to the WB and UR decks' fliers.
Three Festerhide Boar picks in pack 3 produced only two played copies, so the third was a wasted pick; prioritize playable interaction or evasive threats over a redundant common.
Sideboarding Fortress Crab, Moonmist, Naturalize and Pitchburn Devils in before game two preceded our 2-1 win over the BR deck, so plan post-board swaps before round one.
